newsitem.title: UK: British domestic orders rise, exports tumble, survey shows.
newsitem.headline: British domestic orders rise, exports tumble, survey shows.

text.p: Domestic demand for manufacturing goods in Britain rose at its fastest rate for two years in the four months to April, but export orders fell back, the Confederation of British Industry said on Wednesday.
Exports have been undermined by the strength of the pound against major currencies, which makes British goods more expensive abroad.

The CBI's quarterly industrial trends survey showed 31 percent of firms reported rising domestic orders volumes in the last four months while 23 percent said it was down -- leaving a positive balance of eight percent.
"This rate of growth, although below expectations, was the highest in two years," the CBI said.

"By contrast, the balance of seven percent of firms reporting a fall in export orders, represents the sharpest fall since late 1993." Both domestic and, to a lesser extent export orders, were predicted to improve in the next four months.
"These results show that growth has been continuing over the past few months, albeit in moderate fashion," said Andrew Buxton, chairman of the CBI's economic affairs committee.
"The overall manufacturing performance masked a divergent trend in demand. Domestic orders are doing well while demand from overseas is suffering from the continued strength of sterling."
